newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage-backed spreads hold recent tight levels.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage-backed spreads hold recent tight levels.

text.p: Mortgage-backed securities were mostly 1/8 to 1/4 point higher at midday Wednesday, slightly exceeding intermediate Treasuries gains.

After outperforming Treasuries since Friday morning, yield spreads "tightened by a significant amount in the last three days," said one trader. Investors, nonetheless, were not fully insulated from faster prepayments, he said.

"Today, people are focusing more on the 10-year (Treasury note) auction," the trader observed. "But there is stll some danger, certainly in cuspy coupons, of refis," he said, adding mortgage prepayments could exceed some expectations.

Investors who believed they were overly weighted in mortgages might have been planning to turn to the 10-year Treasury note for call protection, participants said. The Treasury was to sell $12 billion of new 10-year notes Wednesday in the second segment of its three-pronged $38 billion refunding this week.

Yield spreads between 30-year mortgage-backed securities and Treasuries tightened by roughly 12 basis points since Friday morning, when unexpectedly strong employment data triggered a massive market downturn.

At midday Wednesday, 30-year Government National Mortgage Association 7 1/2-percent bonds were up 8/32 at 101-11/32 for a bond equivalent yield of 7.32 percent. That yield was 106 basis points above the Treasury 10-year note, which was up 5/32 to yield 6.21 percent.
Among other 30-year 7 1/2-percent issues, Federal National Mortgage Association and Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. bonds were up 6/32 at 101-10/32 and 101-16/32, respectively.

In addition to seeking call protection in Treasuries, the trader said that investors were probably offsetting risk by gathering principal-only securities, which perform well when prepayments rise. Dollar rolls, he said, "are also trading extremely well, 6 1/2s through 8 1/2s."
In a dollar roll transaction, a debtholder sells an MBS pass-through and agrees to buy a substantially identical security on a future data at a specified price.
